help.title: Help
help.overviewText: AI Chess Tutor combines a digital chessboard with a Stockfish analysis engine and an AI tutor that explains your moves. You can optionally connect a physical Chessnut Air board.
help.newGameText: "New game" starts a game against the engine (as White or Black), or records a game between two people at a physical board (OTB). The opponent engine can be chosen in Settings: classic Stockfish with an Elo limit, or Maia for human-like play.
help.tutorText: The tutor automatically comments on your moves (configurable: Silent/Mistakes/Active), answers questions in the chat, and can suggest a move with an explanation on request. This requires an API key from an LLM provider (Settings → LLM tutor).
help.analysisText: The Stockfish analysis shows the three best lines for the current position; the evaluation bar next to the board shows who is ahead. Clicking an analysis line previews it on the board.
help.moveListText: The move list shows the game in figurine notation with error markers (★ best move, ?! inaccuracy, ? mistake, ?? blunder). A move that was undone and then continued differently is kept as a side variation.
help.chessnutText: Use "Connect" at the bottom of the screen to pair a Chessnut Air board over Bluetooth. The LEDs show the last move and correction hints; a toggle lets the best analysis move blink on the board.
help.pgnText: Games can be exported to or imported from PGN ("File" menu); every finished game is also saved automatically to the local library, where it can be reopened later.
help.clockText: A chess clock with tournament presets (Classical/Rapid/Blitz/Bullet) or a free base time/increment can optionally be enabled in Settings.
help.settingsText: The gear icon lets you configure the opponent engine, opening book, chess clock, sound, analysis engine, and the LLM tutor.
help.languageText: Use the flag in the top right to switch the app's language (and the tutor's reply language) at any time.
